ad_library.summary: Solar Apex is running 2 active Meta ads on its Khammam franchise page (facebook.com/61596329420215), both started 4 November 2026. One is a brand ad - phone numbers, the Khammam address and www.solarapex.in - which is in segment for a rooftop-solar installer. The other recruits dealerships, promising Khammam dealers Rs.50,000 to Rs.1 lakh plus a month; that is a different audience and is excluded from the ad count used for this report. The brand ad carries www.solarapex.in as its link, but its CTA button is a WhatsApp message, so the action it pushes is a chat rather than a visit. A third ad the batch-14 run recorded, a hiring ad on the corporate page facebook.com/61575888183929, is no longer in the Ad Library. Google Ads Transparency for solarapex.in returns 0 ads under region=IN, so Meta is the entire paid channel.

funnel.type: WhatsApp CTA, with the site as the ad link
funnel.destination: CTA 'Send WhatsApp message' -> api.whatsapp.com; the ad's own link is www.solarapex.in
funnel.meaning: The ad does point at solarapex.in, so the site is not invisible - but the button the reader is pushed to press opens a WhatsApp conversation instead. Nothing is measurable either way: no pixel firing, no conversion event, no retargeting pool, and no page where a different headline or price could be tested.

findings: The brand ad carries www.solarapex.in as its link, but its CTA button is a WhatsApp message - so the site is in the ad while the action the reader is pushed to take is a chat. Neither route is measurable.

The second live ad recruits dealerships, not customers - it promises Khammam dealers Rs.50,000 to Rs.1 lakh plus a month. Two different audiences are competing inside one ad account, and the recruitment ad is excluded from the count in this report.

The site's header shows info@solarapex.in and +91 96660 05198, but both of those links are wrong on every page: the email href points at info@domain.com and the phone href at +01 248 248 2481, a placeholder. A second block lower down the /contact/ page carries both correctly, so the address is real - it is just one tap away from the version that works.
The ad phone numbers (8125640121, 8008576480) do not match the website phone (+91 96660 05198). Two numbers in market, one on the site, and no way for a customer to tell which is current.

The registered address is Manikonda, Hyderabad 500089, while the advertising page is the Khammam outlet (Church Compound Center). Both are inside Telangana, but the corporate site and the local page are run as separate things.
Zero Google ads under region=IN for solarapex.in, so the whole paid presence is these two Meta ads on one franchise page.
next_steps: Make the site the destination, not the fallback

The brand ad already carries solarapex.in as its link but pushes a WhatsApp CTA. Send it to a real page - offer, subsidy explainer, enquiry form - with a pixel on that page, so the click is measurable and retargetable instead of ending in a chat.
Customer acquisition and dealership recruitment are different buyers with different economics. Separate campaigns, or at minimum separate ads with separate objectives, so neither dilutes the other.

The email link points at info@domain.com and the phone link at +01 248 248 2481, on every page of the site. The /contact/ page already has a working pair lower down - it is a two-line fix in the theme header, and right now it is losing every enquiry that taps instead of reading.
Publish one number that answers, and route the ad numbers to it. Two unmatched numbers in market reads as a company that is hard to reach.

ads_audit.methodology: Control review follows the claude-ads Meta Ads audit catalog (github.com/vamsy16/claude-ads, ads/references/meta-audit.md). Each control is graded only where public evidence establishes it - Ad Library ad data and the lead's own landing page. Controls that require Ads Manager access (bidding, budgets, audiences, learning phase, EMQ, CAPI status) are marked unknown on purpose: they cannot be verified from outside the account and are never guessed.
